1.1: Solomon set the tone early: this book ain't for clout—it's for clarity.
1.2: Wisdom starts when you stop thinking you got it all figured out.
1.3: "Fear of the Lord" don't mean scared of God—it means deep respect + full surrender.
1.7: Fools? They allergic to correction. Can't tell them nothin'.
1.8: Solomon talkin' to his kid—but this advice go for all of us.
1.10: Don't get caught up in street games, fast money, or fake loyalty.
1.16: Some people plot on others and don't realize they really setting a trap for themselves.
1.20: Wisdom ain't hiding. She in the streets, on the timeline, in your DMs—begging folks to listen.
1.24: But people love being hard-headed… until life humbles them.
1.28: When chaos hits, wisdom like, "Don't call me now—you had your chance."
1.31: They hated knowledge and did not choose the fear of the Lord...

2.1: Solomon like, "If you really want wisdom? You gotta hunt for it."
2.2: Not no casual scroll-through. This is dig deep like your life depends on it.
2.3: Wisdom ain't for the lazy. It reveals itself to the hungry.
2.4: And once you go get it, you gon' start to understand the fear of the Lord—which is step one to real insight.
2.6: Wisdom ain't something you manufacture—it comes straight from the Source.
2.7: God got insight, protection, and purpose locked up for the ones walking right.
2.8: It says discretion gon' protect you. Understanding gon' guard you.
2.9: That's grown-people discernment—not everything that glitters is good for you.
2.12: There's folks who plot evil for fun.
2.13: Wisdom gon' spot the deception before you step into it.
2.14: These folks twisted—walking on dark paths, thinking they slick.
2.15: Don't entertain 'em. Don't follow 'em. Don't even flirt with their lifestyle.
2.16: And now Solomon shifts to temptation talk.
2.17: Wisdom gon' keep you from the smooth-talking, curve-throwing, DM-sliding, "I'm different" type...
2.18: But they ain't rooted in God.
2.19: Messin' with them? Leads to dead ends—emotionally, spiritually, sometimes physically.
2.20: Wisdom ain't just about avoiding drama—it's about choosing the right legacy.
2.21: The upright? They get stability. The faithful? They stay planted.
2.22: The wicked? Eventually removed—no roots, no fruit.

3.1: Solomon like, "Don't just hear this—keep it."
3.2: God's wisdom ain't for your memory—it's for your character.
3.3: Living by it brings favor with both God and people. That's spiritual and social clout.
3.5: One of the coldest bars in the Bible.
3.6: God ain't ask for 50% trust—He said all your heart.
3.7: That "lean not" part? Means stop trying to reason through everything. Sometimes God's way won't make sense—but it works.
3.8: If you acknowledge Him, He gon' direct your steps. Not maybe—He will.
3.9: Thinking you got it all figured out? That's how folks end up hurt.
3.10: True reverence brings healing—not just spiritually, but physically.
3.11: Some stress in your body ain't about your diet—it's about your disobedience.
3.12: God don't just want lip service—He wants you to honor Him with your resources too.
3.13: Give Him the first, not the leftovers.
3.14: The result? Overflow. Provision. Full barns, new wine—it's legacy harvest.
3.15: That rebuke you felt? That closed door? That hard lesson?
3.17: God corrects His kids 'cause He wants better for them—not 'cause He petty.
3.18: Wisdom ain't just smart—it's spiritual wealth.
3.19: It brings peace, favor, and long life.
3.20: God used wisdom to create everything. So imagine what it could do in you.
3.21: You don't have to walk around scared or second-guessing everything.
3.22: Wisdom brings stability. You sleep better, walk bolder, live lighter.
3.23: No fear of sudden disaster—God already mapped out your moves.
3.27: If you got it, give it. Don't stall generosity.
3.28: Stop actin' like you broke in your spirit when God made you rich in kindness.
3.29: Also, keep the peace. Don't start no mess if they didn't bring none to your door.
3.31: Don't envy evil just 'cause it look successful. That shine temporary.
3.32: The humble gon' inherit honor. The wicked gon' catch shade from the Lord Himself.
3.33: God playing the long game—and wisdom always wins.

4.1: Solomon like, "Look, I ain't just saying this—I heard it from my father too."
4.2: David passed it to Solomon. Solomon now passing it to you.
4.3: Wisdom is an inheritance. You don't just flex it, you protect it.
4.4: She'll promote you, honor you, crown you—if you value her.
4.10: Solomon is like, "You don't gotta guess your next move—wisdom clears the path."
4.11: When you walk with her, you don't stumble.
4.12: "Hold on to instruction"—like it's your lifeline. 'Cause it is.
4.14: Solomon ain't sugarcoating: "Stay away from them streets."
4.15: Wicked folks can't even sleep till they cause chaos.
4.16: Their path is darkness—they don't even know why they keep stumbling.
4.20: THIS the anchor verse. "Above all else"? That means don't play with this part.
4.21: Your heart is headquarters. If it's messy, your mouth messy, your moves messy, your mindset messy.
4.22: Then he adds: watch your mouth, keep your eyes straight, and don't swerve.

5.1: Solomon starting with a red flag warning. That sweet talk? That slick talk?
5.2: It sound good, feel good—but ends bitter and sharp.
5.3: She don't care about your soul. Her steps don't lead to purpose—they lead to the pit.
5.4: And she don't even realize how lost she is.
5.7: Solomon don't say "be careful"—he says don't even go near.
5.8: 'Cause if you entertain it, next thing you know, your strength, your money, your years, your peace—gone.
5.9: "At the end of your life you'll groan..." That's regret talk.
5.10: Regret be loud when wisdom was quieted early.
5.15: Solomon now talking grown. He say, be faithful to your spouse.
5.16: What's yours is enough. Pour into your own well.
5.17: Let love be fresh, wild, and satisfying—but keep it sacred.
5.18: "Why spill your water in the streets?" Don't waste what's meant to be intimate.
5.21: Even when you think nobody saw it—God did.
5.22: And Solomon says a person gets caught up in their own mess—like a trap they set for themselves.
5.23: Discipline was lacking, so destruction was waiting.

6.1: Solomon's sayin', "Be careful signing on for somebody else's mess."
6.2: You co-signin' credit, loans, favors—and now you locked in.
6.3: If you did it? Move quick, humble yourself, and get out that deal.
6.4: Cause if they can't cover it—you paying for it.
6.7: The ant don't need a boss—it just moves. Stores up in the summer so it don't struggle in winter.
6.8: But the sluggard? Always sayin' "5 more minutes"—next thing you know, poverty crept in like a thief.
6.12: Solomon describing that person who lives in drama. Always stirring the pot, always got a side eye, always plotting.
6.13: He said disaster gon' snap on them fast—no warning.
6.17: There are six things the Lord hates, seven that are detestable to Him: 1. Haughty eyes – That arrogant, "I'm better than you" spirit. 2. A lying tongue – Straight up dishonesty. 3. Hands that shed innocent blood – Hurting people who ain't done nothin'.
6.18: 4. A heart that devises wicked schemes – Always scheming in the dark. 5. Feet that rush into evil – Quick to pull up for mess but slow to show up for righteousness.
6.19: 6. A false witness who pours out lies – Ain't just lying—they lying on somebody else. 7. A person who stirs up conflict in the community – The biggest red flag: someone who loves drama more than peace.
6.20: Solomon like, "Don't leave the wisdom you learned from mama and daddy."
6.21: Let it ride with you day and night.
6.22: It'll protect you from temptation, manipulation, and smooth talkers.
6.25: Solomon circling back to sexual temptation.
6.26: That attraction might feel natural, but if it's outside of God's will, it's fire with no boundaries.
6.27: Can you scoop fire to your chest and not get burned? Nah.
6.28: Same with someone else's spouse or situationships that steal your peace.
6.30: You steal some food when you starving? Folks might understand.
6.32: It brings shame, jealousy, and wounds you might never fully heal from.

7.1: Solomon like, "Treat wisdom like family. Keep her close." 'Cause there's a whole world out here tryna finesse you. Wisdom keeps you from getting caught up with the smooth-talking, curve-throwin', soul-snatching type.
7.6: Solomon straight narrating like a movie now. "I was chillin', lookin' out my window, and I saw this young dude... clueless." No direction, no discernment—just vibes and vulnerability. And what time is it? Nighttime. Foolishness don't wait for daylight.
7.10: She ain't just dressed for attention—she got a plan. Loud, bold, smooth. Ain't waiting on no invitation—she outside and active. She grabs him. Initiates. Aggressive with it.
7.14: She talkin' religious to build trust: "I just got back from church." "I've been lookin' just for you." She paints the perfect vibe: soft bed, perfume, privacy. And the kicker? "My husband's outta town, he took the bag, won't be back for a while..."
7.21: She ain't yelling. She persuading. Whispering. Convincing. And he follows—no hesitation. Not knowing it's his downfall walk. Solomon compares him to a cow getting led to the butcher. That's heavy. Arrow to the liver = death. That's what unchecked lust leads to.
7.24: Solomon not tryna scare you—he tryna save you. This ain't her first time. She's done this before. And there's bodies behind her charm. That house? That room? That situation? It's a straight highway to hell.

8.1: Wisdom ain't whisperin'. She up high, in the streets, at the crossroads, callin' out to everybody. She like, "Y'all keep actin' like I'm hard to find, but I been hollerin'." And who she talking to? You. The simple, the clueless, the unwise. She tryna help, not judge. And she ain't offering fluff—she serving truth, clarity, and understanding better than any bag, better than diamonds.
8.12: Wisdom saying, "I'm not just smart—I'm strategic." She got discernment, creativity, and protection. She helps kings reign, judges rule, bosses lead, and everyday people walk upright. She don't just bring insight—she brings inheritance. She says: "I walk with justice and I make your life rich."
8.22: This where it gets deep. Wisdom saying, "I was here before the world started." Before oceans, before mountains, before the skies—Wisdom was there. She ain't created on accident. God birthed her on purpose—as the blueprint. Wisdom was right beside God, rejoicing as He formed everything. That's OG energy.
8.32: Wisdom shifts tone. Now she mama-bearin' us. "Listen to me. Watch my steps. Don't just hear—obey." She promises: follow me = blessing, favor, life. But turn away from me? That's self-harm. "Whoever hates me loves death." That's blunt… and it's real.

9.1: Lady Wisdom ain't lazy. She put in work. House built solid. Table set. Food seasoned. Wine poured. And she ain't keepin' it exclusive—she callin' out to everybody, even the simple: "Come eat. Come learn. Leave your foolishness at the door." It's a full-course meal of insight, correction, and life.
9.7: Solomon drops a side note here: "Some folks don't want wisdom—they want smoke." If they not teachable, correction becomes conflict. But a wise person? They love feedback. They grow from it. Don't waste your oil on folks who want attention, not transformation.
9.10: This line hit like a chorus that keep coming back. Want real wisdom? Start with reverence. Not fear like terror—fear like deep awe and submission. Wisdom benefits you. But if you reject it? That loss is on you, too.
9.13: Here come Lady Folly. Loud, ignorant, reckless—but real persuasive. She callin' out too, same way Wisdom did. But her words? Lies with a cherry on top. "Stolen water is sweet..." Translation: "It's more fun when it's wrong." But what she ain't sayin'? Everybody inside that house is spiritually dead. Straight-up graveyard vibes.

10.1: Solomon kickin' off with family impact. Your choices ain't just about you—they ripple into your household. Wisdom uplifts. Foolishness breaks hearts.
10.2: Fast money without integrity? Worthless in the long run. God don't just bless stuff—He blesses the righteous. He makes sure you don't starve, spiritually or naturally.
10.4: This one right here? Motivation. If you sit around waiting on it—you gon' miss the whole harvest. Wisdom shows up early and puts in work.
10.6: The righteous get remembered with love. The wicked? Their name fade quick—no honor, no legacy.
10.8: Wisdom listens before it speaks. The foolish talk loud, ignore correction, and walk into their own downfall. Integrity = security. Lies = exposure.
10.10: Solomon say even subtle shade (winks, sarcasm, side talk) can spark conflict. But a righteous mouth? It gives life. Encourages. Uplifts. Fools speak reckless and end up exposed.
10.15: Money can protect you, but it can't replace wisdom or discipline. Corrected people live longer. Rebellious folks self-sabotage.
10.18: Haters lie. They pretend it's peace when it's really poison. Righteous people don't fake—they speak what builds. Fools talk a lot and say nothing.
10.22: God's favor don't grind you into dust. When He blesses, He sustains. No drama, no anxiety, no regret. Peaceful provision > stressed success.
10.23: Wicked folks get short wins—but the righteous get long-term legacy. Fear of the Lord? Brings security, joy, and longevity. The wicked keep gettin' removed. The righteous? They stay planted.

11.1: God ain't feelin' fraud. Whether it's business, backroom deals, or sneaky behavior—He sees all that. Integrity in the small things? That's how you gain His favor.
11.2: Pride always sets you up for a fall. But humble folks? They stay learning, stay growing, stay winning.
11.3: Integrity is like GPS—it'll keep you from turning down the wrong roads. The wicked stay schemin', but it always boomerangs back.
11.7: If all your hope is in people or in shady gains, it's dead on arrival. The righteous? God always provides a way out.
11.9: Some folks talk slick and tear down communities. The righteous speak life—and their wisdom brings escape, safety, and peace. Even cities get lifted when real ones lead.
11.13: If they tellin' everybody else's business to you, they probably tellin' your business to everybody else. God honors the ones who can be trusted in silence.
11.14: Solo moves sound strong, but wise moves come from godly advice. Even kings need counsel. Even visionaries need guidance.
11.17: Every act of kindness comes back blessed. But cruelty, pettiness, and cold-heartedness? It always folds inward.
11.21: Don't get discouraged when it looks like evil folks winnin'. They not. Justice don't miss—it might take time, but it always shows up.
11.22: Solomon not dissin' beauty—he's sayin' without wisdom and discretion, it's wasted. Outer beauty can't cover up inner mess. Real value's in the mindset, not just the makeup.
11.24: God's math don't match the world's: the more you give, the more you gain. Stingy folks stay stuck. Givers stay supplied. Bless the people—and watch God bless you.
11.27: Seek good, find good. Chase righteousness, walk in favor. God is fair, and everybody gon' reap what they sow.

12.1: Solomon said what he said. If you reject correction? You ain't just wrong—you actin' foolish. Growth ain't always comfortable, but it's necessary. Correction is love in work clothes.
12.2: Righteous folks get divine favor. God backs them. Wicked folks might look successful, but they ain't built solid. No root = no fruit that lasts.
12.4: This ain't gender-locked—it's truth for everybody: the right partner is a crown, the wrong one is corrosion. You wanna thrive in life? Choose someone with character, not just charisma.
12.5: Righteous people ain't just out here wingin' it—they move with purpose and justice. Wicked plans might run hot—but they burn out fast. Truth got stamina. Lies run outta gas.
12.8: Translation: Live in your means. Eat in peace. Don't go broke tryna look rich. God honors the humble, not the hype beast.
12.10: If you righteous, even how you treat your pets says somethin'. And if you put in work? You gon' eat. Dreamin' don't feed you—discipline does.
12.12: Jealousy got folks chasing what they didn't plant. But the righteous? They focus on their lane—and the fruit comes naturally.
12.15: Fools react. The wise reflect. Some things don't deserve your energy. Silence is often the real flex.
12.17: Solomon stay on this theme—truth has weight. Lies may win attention, but never God's approval. Real ones stay solid, even when it ain't popular.
12.23: You ain't gotta announce every move—just make it matter. Diligence leads to promotion. Righteousness leads to life—not just existing, but thriving.

13.1: Wise people lean in and listen. Fools just clap back, roll their eyes, or ghost when correction comes.
13.2: Your words shape your world. Talking reckless = self-sabotage. Wise people talk with purpose. Fools talk outta pocket.
13.4: Lazy folks stay hungry. They want the reward but not the routine. The diligent? They feast off what they actually worked for.
13.5: The righteous stay allergic to fake. Wicked folks might win short-term, but the stink always rise to the surface. Integrity is armor—you wear it or regret it.
13.7: Don't let looks fool you. Broke folks be flexin', while the real wealthy stay quiet and invested. Wealth ain't just numbers—it's discipline and wisdom.
13.9: Pride causes drama. Simple. The wise listen, learn, and adjust. That's how peace grows and purpose flows.
13.11: Scams, get-rich-quick plays, fast bags—they all dry up. But steady stacking? That's God's rhythm.
13.12: Waiting on breakthrough too long can wear your soul down. But when God comes through? Whew—it hits different. That's the kind of joy that makes you stand taller.
13.13: Ignoring instruction? That'll cost you. But wise moves? They bring respect and reward. Life runs smoother when you stop swerving around God's will.
13.16: Wise folks think before they act. Fools act then wonder why they fell. Discipline may sting in the moment—but it'll save your future.
13.19: Energy contagious. Vibes rub off. If you hang with fools, don't be shocked when life gets foolish. Wisdom spreads the same way—choose your circle carefully.
13.22: Righteous folks don't just live right—they leave right. It's bigger than you—it's about the next generation. And God makes sure they're fed, fulfilled, and favored.

14.1: Solomon starts off real blunt. A wise woman invests, nurtures, protects—she builds legacy. A foolish one? Wrecks everything she touches—relationships, peace, foundation.
14.2: Prideful people pop off quick. Wise folks know when to speak and when to shut up. Sometimes silence is your safest defense.
14.4: Translation: If you want growth, you gon' have to deal with some mess. Productivity ain't always clean. But no mess? That probably means no movement.
14.5: If they lying, scheming, and spinning stories, why are you still listening? Wisdom knows when to walk away—not entertain foolishness.
14.8: Wise people pause and think before they move. Fools out here wingin' it, then lyin' when it goes left.
14.10: Everybody got a story behind the smile. You can't fully feel what someone else is going through—so be gentle with people.
14.11: Just 'cause it feels right, looks right, or sounds right don't mean it is. Check the fruit, not just the vibe. Your gut can't lead you better than God.
14.13: Wise people move with discernment. Fools stay ready to pop off but swear they safe. Wisdom ain't scared—it's just strategic.
14.17: If you always triggered, you easy to play. Anger unchecked becomes regret you gotta live with. The patient? They always end up on top.
14.20: God don't play about the poor, the overlooked, the vulnerable. Kindness ain't weakness—it's what attracts favor.
14.22: Doing right ain't always glamorous—but it's rewarding. God's wisdom preserves you. Working hard, loving deep, walking clean? That's the path to peace and purpose.
14.28: Great leaders have loyal people—but bad character loses influence fast. Envy rots the bones. Wisdom gives strength. Kindness to the poor = honor. Oppression = shame. A wise servant gets promoted. A foolish one? Left behind.

15.1: You got power in your tone. A soft word can de-escalate drama. A loud one can ignite it. Don't match energy—master it.
15.2: Wise people build people up. Fools just talk to hear themselves. Your words can refresh folks or wreck 'em. The tongue is either a tool or a trap.
15.5: A fool thinks correction = control. But real wisdom knows correction = love and protection. Some of the best moves you'll ever make come after someone checked you.
15.6: God ain't impressed by fake worship or outward gestures. He sees the life behind the lip service. Righteous living = divine favor.
15.10: The path got guardrails called correction. Ignore 'em? You crash. Fools hate feedback. Wise folks seek it.
15.13: Joy on the inside eventually shows on the outside. But if your heart broken? Even sunny days feel cloudy. Wisdom knows how to guard peace internally.
15.16: Solomon droppin' lifestyle goals here. A little + peace + God > a lot + chaos + ego. Peace is the real bag.
15.18: It ain't strength to pop off—it's wisdom to hold back. Patience is power. A calm spirit keeps the room from blowin' up.
15.22: You need real ones around you who speak life and logic. Don't plan in isolation—get insight. Counsel is confirmation before chaos.
15.23: Some words hit different when they're timely. Wise folks lift people up with their words. Discernment gives direction and elevation.
15.25: God don't bless pride. He don't bless dirty money either. The humble? Protected. The greedy? Always end up losing more than they gain.
15.28: Righteous folks think before they speak. Fools shoot off emotionally, then try to apologize after the damage. Wisdom grows from reverence, and elevation walks through humility.

16.1: You can plan, strategize, make vision boards—cool. But if you ain't invited God in, your path ain't grounded. "Commit" = hand it over. Not just ask God to bless it—build it with Him.
16.4: God sees everything, and it all folds into His will—even the messy parts. And He got smoke for the prideful—He said it's detestable. That's strong.
16.6: Love + faithfulness = that grace combo. When your walk is upright, even your enemies start chillin'. A little with peace > a lot with pressure.
16.9: This is the anchor verse. We plan—but God fine-tunes every footstep. Walk with Him, not ahead of Him.
16.10: When a king (or boss, or parent, or CEO) moves wisely, people thrive. But when leadership is off? The whole body suffers.
16.16: Wisdom outlasts money. And humility gets you access money can't buy. Pride and quick gains might look fun—but it ain't stable.
16.20: Wisdom ain't just about knowing—it's about listening. And when you speak from that place? Your words heal, not hurt.
16.25: Just 'cause it feels good don't mean it's God. Double check your direction before you wreck your destiny.
16.26: Hunger makes folks hustle—but without direction, you grind in circles. Wicked folks stir drama and speak death. Avoid folks who wink, whisper, and work wickedness behind closed doors.
16.31: Long life lived well = legacy. Self-control is better than flexin' strength. And even the dice roll? God's hand decides what hits.

17.1: Solomon starting with priorities: Peace > Plates. You can have a big house, full fridge, and still be miserable if it's filled with drama. Peace ain't luxury—it's necessity.
17.2: God promotes character, not just bloodlines or positions. A loyal worker will outshine an entitled child. Legacy don't make you worthy—loyalty and wisdom do.
17.3: You get purified through pressure. God ain't punishing you—He refining you. And He checks hearts, not headlines.
17.4: Don't entertain gossip, slander, or shade—it corrupts you too. And don't clown folks goin' through it—God sees how you treat the low.
17.6: Grandkids = generational crown. Parents who live right give their kids someone to honor, not hide. Legacy ain't just money—it's how you're remembered.
17.7: Real love don't replay the mistake—it forgives and covers. Gossip spreads pain. Grace restores peace. You ain't loyal if you always loud when someone messes up.
17.10: The wise feel correction in one sentence. A fool can go through 100 consequences and still not change.
17.11: Evil folks chase rebellion—don't entertain that. Starting conflict is like bustin' a dam—hard to stop once it's out. God hates when wrong is called right, and right is called wrong.
17.17: Fair-weather friends leave when it gets tough. But real ones? They show up stronger in the storm. They not just around—they're built for it.
17.18: Solomon stay warning: don't cosign people's foolishness. If they ain't wise with theirs, don't attach your name to it.
17.21: Quiet don't mean clueless—it can mean controlled. Fools love to talk. The wise love to listen and discern. Loud don't mean right. Volume ain't wisdom.

18.1: Some folks isolate and say, "I don't need nobody." Nah—that's pride, not protection. Avoiding people might feel safe, but it also blocks growth. And usually, folks isolatin' got drama brewin'.
18.2: Fools ain't tryna learn—they tryna be loud. They don't want the truth, they just want the mic. All talk, no transformation.
18.4: Real wisdom ain't shallow—it nourishes like a fresh spring. When wise folks speak, there's depth. They don't just answer questions—they pour perspective.
18.6: Fools don't get jumped—they run their mouth into danger. They set themselves up with every word. No filter, no peace.
18.8: Gossip be juicy—but it rots from the inside out. You might feel informed, but you're really being infected.
18.9: Laziness don't just hold you back—it destroys opportunity. You either building or breaking. There's no in-between.
18.10: God's name ain't just spiritual—it's protection. When life gets real, the real ones run to Him—not distractions, not denial.
18.11: Rich folks think their money protects them—but it's a false sense of security. Wealth can't save you from loss, heartbreak, or eternity.
18.12: Pride always walks in before the fall. But humility opens doors pride would've slammed shut.
18.13: If you respond before you fully hear, you already wrong. Wisdom waits. Fools react.
18.14: A strong spirit can push through pain. But once your spirit breaks? Even your body can't carry you. Guard your heart. Nurture your joy.
18.15: Wisdom don't stop learning. They're always leanin' in, takin' notes, asking better questions.
18.16: Your gift might get you in the room. But if your character ain't right, you won't stay there. Favor is fast—integrity lasts.
18.17: That "he said/she said" be soundin' convincing—until you get the full picture. Don't rush to defend or cancel—get context.
18.20: Words are weapons. Words are seeds. Words are mirrors. You are what you speak repeatedly—to others and to yourself.
18.22: A solid spouse ain't just fine—they're favor in human form. Marriage is legacy work. Choose with God, not just chemistry.
18.24: Large crowds ain't deep connections. Real friends don't dip when it's dark. They lean in. Jesus is that ultimate Friend—and He sticks regardless.

19.1: Don't let poverty make you think you're less. You'd rather have peace and principles than riches with no respect. Being broke ain't the worst—being foul with it is.
19.2: Passion without wisdom = problems. Rushing leads to wrong turns and regrets. And when people mess up, they wanna blame God? Nah—that's you.
19.4: Solomon lettin' you know: loyalty gets tested in hard times. People love what you have—not always who you are. But the ones who stay? Those are the ones sent from God.
19.8: Wisdom is an investment in your own life. It pays back in peace, provision, and purpose. But lies? Lies get exposed. Every time.
19.10: Don't chase positions you ain't ready to carry. When fools get money or power, things crumble. But patience and humility? That's how God raises folks up.
19.13: You can inherit money, status, property... But a real, wise, God-sent spouse? That's heaven's favor. And a nagging one? That's like drip torture daily. Oof.
19.15: Lazy people sleep on opportunities—literally. But when you give to the poor, God sees that as a loan to Himself. And trust—He pays back with interest.
19.18: Letting kids wild out without correction? That ain't love—it's neglect. Correction brings life. Rebellion left unchecked brings pain. And grown folks? Still need correction too.
19.21: You got vision, ideas, dreams. Cool. But God got blueprint, timing, and purpose. If your plan don't line up with His? It ain't gon' stick.
19.22: God honors real over rich, and truth over talk. If you ignore wisdom long enough, life gon' teach you the hard way. Consequences ain't canceled just 'cause you didn't believe them.

20.1: Ain't sayin' you can't sip, but if the bottle controlling you? That's a problem. Alcohol'll have you talkin' slick, moving reckless, and blaming the liquor when it's really you. Wisdom knows the limit—and when to say no.
20.2: Solomon say it clear: Don't go lookin' for smoke. Real strength is being able to walk away when it ain't worth it. Only fools gotta prove a point every time.
20.4: Lazy folks skip the planting but still expect blessings? Nah. No grind = no harvest. It's really that simple.
20.5: Don't just listen to what folks say—discern what they mean. Wise folks don't judge fast—they ask, observe, and listen deeper.
20.6: Talk is cheap. Loyalty is rare. Don't get hyped off promises—watch their patterns.
20.7: The way you live now sets the tone for your bloodline. Your name carries weight—good or bad.
20.9: Ain't nobody sinless—but you can be honest about it. God works with transparency, not self-righteousness.
20.10: Don't be shady with people in business or in life. God sees how you handle fairness behind closed doors.
20.12: Not everybody got spiritual ears and eyes open. Wisdom starts when you realize God gave you both to use.
20.13: Sleep ain't bad—but lovin' it too much will steal your bag. Work while it's time to work.
20.15: You can't buy wisdom with money. When someone speaks truth and life—that's treasure.
20.17: Sinful wins feel good for a moment—but they burn later. You can't cheat your way to purpose.
20.18: Get advice before moves. Don't rush revenge—it's God's job, not yours. Move strategic, not petty.
20.24: You ain't gotta have it all figured out. Let God guide. He sees the turns you don't.
20.27: God don't just check your actions—He checks your soul. Your spirit don't lie, even when your words do.

21.1: Even the most powerful person ain't outside God's reach. God can shift hearts, reroute agendas, and override power plays.
21.2: Just because it makes sense to you don't mean it's righteous. God ain't just checking behavior—He's reading what's underneath.
21.3: God ain't moved by performance—He wants consistent obedience. Don't give big and live reckless. Live right then give.
21.4: Pride and greed always grow sin. When your eyes high and your heart hard, the soil of your life stays dry.
21.5: Rushing ain't riches. Fast money fades. Steady moves stack over time.
21.6: Fraud money feels good now—but it's cursed. What you lie to get, you'll eventually lose or regret.
21.9: It ain't gendered—it's principle: peace in your space matters. A beautiful house with constant drama is a spiritual prison.
21.13: God takes how you treat the struggling personal. If you cold to the broken, don't expect warmth when you hit the wall.
21.14: Sometimes a quiet blessing brings more healing than public gestures. Real generosity ain't loud—it's strategic and spirit-led.
21.16: Wandering from wisdom ain't neutral—it's deadly. You may not see it right away, but your peace and purpose suffer fast.
21.21: You want the real wins? Chase what's right. Righteousness leads to life. Not just survival—abundant life.
21.23: You ain't gotta comment on everything. Guard your mouth like your future depends on it—because it does.
21.25: Lazy people stay dreaming, never doing. Desires without discipline become disappointment.
21.30: You can plot, scheme, strategize—but if God ain't in it? It's not gon' last. Victory belongs to the Lord. He got the final word.

22.1: Don't just build a bag—build a reputation. People might forget what you wore, but they'll never forget how you carried yourself. A solid name opens doors money can't.
22.2: Money don't change the fact that we all got the same Creator. Don't look down on nobody. You ain't better—you just blessed differently.
22.3: Wisdom got eyes. She peeps game early and pivots. Fools act like they can't see red flags—until it's too late.
22.4: Stay low and reverent—God elevates the humble. Honor, wealth, peace—it flows from surrender, not self-promotion.
22.6: Raise them in truth, even if they wild out for a season. Seeds don't always sprout fast—but they still grow. Foundation matters more than perfection.
22.7: Debt looks convenient till it owns you. Freedom ain't just spiritual—it's financial wisdom too.
22.9: Stingy folks stay empty. Givers stay filled. God always blesses the open-handed.
22.10: Peace ain't possible when messy folks are still in the mix. You don't fix chaos—you remove the instigator.
22.11: Clean heart + wise words = divine connections. People in high places trust those with real integrity.
22.13: Lazy folks always got a reason why they ain't moved yet. Fear, fake scenarios, blame—it's all stall tactics.
22.17: Don't just hear wisdom—absorb it. Let it shape how you walk, talk, trust, and move.
22.22: Mistreat the broken? You just picked a fight with God. He steps in for the ones nobody else fights for.
22.24: Bad temper spreads like smoke. Stay too close and you gon' smell like it. Your crew shapes your character.
22.29: Real skill don't need to chase recognition—it pulls it naturally. Master your craft. Do it like it's ministry.

23.1: That VIP invite ain't always a blessing—it could be a trap. Watch who you're eating with. That favor might come with fine print. You sitting at the table… but are you the meal?
23.4: Grinding ain't bad—but worshipping wealth will wreck you. Money moves fast. Don't kill yourself chasin' what can disappear overnight.
23.6: If they don't rock with you for real, don't accept their fake love. Just 'cause they offer you something don't mean they mean it. God sees hearts—and so should you.
23.9: You can't force-feed truth to somebody who already decided to ignore it. Every ear ain't ready. Every heart ain't open.
23.10: That means don't exploit the vulnerable—especially the fatherless and poor. God Himself steps in as their lawyer and judge.
23.12: Wisdom ain't passive—you gotta press into it. Focused heart. Open ears. That's how growth happens.
23.13: Correction ain't cruelty—it's protection. Letting kids wild out with no consequences? That's what's actually dangerous.
23.15: Solomon speaking like a real dad. A wise child ain't just successful—they're a blessing to their family's name.
23.17: Just 'cause they shining now don't mean it's real light. Your story still unfolding. Keep your eyes on purpose, not their profile.
23.19: Overindulgence leads to ruin. Discipline keeps you upright. The undisciplined stay broke, tired, and stuck.
23.22: Respect your mama and daddy—especially when they age. Wise living = the kind of child that makes parents proud and God pleased.
23.26: Solomon's beggin': Watch where your heart goes, not just your body. Seduction leads to traps, trauma, and soul ties. Lust looks good—but it don't lead nowhere good.
23.29: Solomon paints a full picture of drunkenness: regret, confusion, pain, loss. The problem ain't the sip—it's when it becomes your escape plan.

24.1: Just 'cause they winnin' don't mean they blessed. Some folks get it dirty and stay lookin' over their shoulder. You don't know what demons come with their lifestyle.
24.3: You don't build a real life off vibes—you build it off wisdom. A solid foundation ain't loud—it's intentional. Don't just chase aesthetics. Build with substance.
24.5: Strong people ain't solo—they move with wise counsel. You want to win? Surround yourself with strategic, spirit-filled people.
24.7: Fools stay loud in the wrong rooms—but quiet when wisdom shows up. Wisdom ain't just knowing—it's knowing when to speak and when to sit still.
24.10: Anybody can look strong when life is sweet. But when pressure hits? Your real faith shows up—or folds.
24.11: Don't stay silent while others suffer. God sees when we pretend not to see. Speak up. Step in. Be the one who protects what's right.
24.13: Wisdom ain't just practical—it's nourishing. The more you walk in it, the more your life tastes like peace.
24.15: Righteous folks stumble too—but they don't stay down. The difference between failure and defeat? Bounce-back. God don't expect perfection—He honors persistence.
24.17: Don't celebrate other people's downfall—even if they hurt you. Vengeance don't make you holy—it makes you small. God got that covered.
24.19: Evil might shine short-term—but it burns out quick. Keep walkin' with God. His light stays on forever.
24.23: Real ones don't switch up truth based on clout, status, or pressure. Fairness is God's language. Speak what's right—even when it's uncomfortable.
24.27: Don't build the dream before you prep the ground. Foundation before flair. Strategy before spotlight.
24.28: Revenge culture ain't kingdom culture. You can't walk with God and live petty.

25.1: Solomon's words had so much weight, folks came back generations later to write 'em down again. Real wisdom don't expire—it evolves with you.
25.2: God don't hide wisdom from you—He hides it for you. Leaders dig. They ask deeper questions. They ain't satisfied with surface.
25.4: You want your life to shine? Cut the mess out. A strong leader don't tolerate shady circles. Purity brings clarity—and authority.
25.6: Don't force a seat at the table—let God pull the chair out. Self-promotion is loud. Humility gets invited.
25.8: Don't be quick to sue, accuse, or expose. Handle things quietly and wisely—protect everybody's dignity.
25.11: Words hit different when they're timely. Wisdom ain't just truth—it's truth wrapped in grace and timing.
25.13: Trustworthy people are rare and refreshing. In pressure seasons, real ones bring clarity—not confusion.
25.14: Don't promise what you ain't about to deliver. Hype with no follow-through just builds disappointment.
25.15: You don't need to shout to shift a room. Patience + wisdom will move people power can't.
25.16: Too much of a good thing can turn toxic. Even blessings need boundaries. And even close friends need space.
25.18: Lying, joking insensitively, dismissing pain—it hurts more than it helps. Wisdom is empathetic, not just clever.
25.21: Don't match hate—out-love it. Your kindness exposes their character and elevates yours.
25.25: Encouragement in hard seasons is life-giving. Be the one who brings hope, not just headlines.
25.26: When you bend to wrong just to blend in, your witness gets cloudy. People thirsty for truth can't drink from muddy water.

27.1: You can plan—but don't get cocky. Life can flip real quick. Move with humility.
27.2: Real ones don't need to self-promote. If it's solid, others will speak on it. If you always the one gassin' yourself, it starts feelin' like insecurity dressed as confidence.
27.3: Dealin' with fools will drain you. They don't just act up—they pull you into their chaos.
27.4: Jealousy ain't loud—it's lowkey lethal. That's why it's more dangerous than anger—it hides, schemes, and plots.
27.5: True friends check you outta love, not hate. They don't gas you up when you wildin'—they pull you back in line.
27.7: When your soul starving, you'll call anything a blessing—even if it's toxic. Hungry hearts settle. Full ones discern.
27.9: The right word from the right one? Life-giving. Some friends just hit different 'cause they know how to pour into you when you empty.
27.10: When life hits, it's the present people who matter most—not just blood, but availability and love.
27.12: God gave you discernment for a reason. Wisdom moves out the way. Fools press in then play victim.
27.17: If your circle ain't helping you grow, you dullin' together. Real friends challenge and refine, not just chill and agree.
27.19: You can fake it for a while, but your heart will leak. What you value, feel, believe—it all shows up in how you live.
27.21: Compliments test you just like criticism. If praise makes you prideful, you ain't ready for promotion.
27.23: Wisdom isn't just about deep quotes—it's responsibility, stewardship, and daily consistency.

28.1: If you livin' foul, you stay lookin' over your shoulder. But when your heart clean? You move different. Confident. Covered. Clear.
28.2: Too many hands on the wheel = disorder. But one wise, spirit-led leader can stabilize the whole ship.
28.4: If you ignore truth, you naturally side with foolishness. But wisdom trains your spirit to spot—and reject—evil moves.
28.6: God ain't impressed by your bag—He's watching your walk. Money don't clean up character.
28.9: You can't ignore God's voice all day, then expect Him to pick up at night. Obedience keeps the line open.
28.13: You don't heal what you hide. Mercy's waiting—but you gotta bring it to light first.
28.14: A soft heart hears God. A hard heart hears pride. Stay sensitive, not stubborn.
28.18: What you walk in now decides what you walk into later. You can't run shady and expect to land safe.
28.19: Dreamin' don't feed you. Diligence does. Wisdom stays consistent, not distracted.
28.20: God blesses loyalty over hustle-for-hype. Fast money got fast consequences.
28.22: Greedy folks think they winnin'—but God already saw the trap ahead. You can't outrun what you refuse to repent for.
28.23: Flattery feeds feelings. Correction feeds growth. A real friend checks you, then walks with you.
28.25: Not every "inner voice" is God. The heart lies. The Spirit leads.

29.1: God don't keep repeating Himself forever. You keep dodging wisdom? At some point, consequences gon' catch you.
29.2: Leadership ain't just policy—it's presence and posture. When leaders love justice, the people breathe easier. When they wicked? Everybody suffers.
29.5: Not every compliment is clean. Some folks hype you up just to trap you later.
29.6: Sin always got strings. But righteousness? It moves free, light, and joyful.
29.7: Don't say you love God but ignore the hurting, broken, and overlooked. Justice is love in public.
29.9: Fools don't want truth—they want to win the argument. Wisdom don't waste breath where peace ain't possible.
29.11: Just 'cause you feel it don't mean you gotta say it. Real maturity is knowing when to hold your fire.
29.15: Parents who don't discipline? Raise kids the world gotta correct. Love teaches, trains, and checks before consequences come knocking.
29.18: Without God's vision, folks move reckless. When you got purpose? It grounds you, guides you, and grows you.
29.20: Talking fast don't mean you know something. Slow down. Listen. Think. Then speak.
29.22: Anger opens the door to actions you can't take back. Wisdom doesn't explode—it processes then proceeds.
29.23: You don't gotta push yourself up—God does the lifting when you stay low. Pride wants attention. Humility earns respect.
29.25: People-pleasing is exhausting. You can't run with God and stay stuck in approval addiction.

30.1: Agur starts honest: "I ain't the smartest. I'm tired. But I fear God." That posture? That's how real wisdom begins. You don't have to know it all—just know who to lean on.
30.4: Agur askin' real questions. "Who really got this whole thing on lock?" Answer: God—and His Son. This a sneak peek of Jesus before the New Testament even drops.
30.5: You don't gotta remix God's Word—it's already perfect and precise. Addin' your own spin? Dangerous. Let the truth be truth.
30.7: This right here? Balance prayer. He's sayin': "God, don't give me too little that I gotta sin, or too much that I forget You." That's real self-awareness and trust.
30.10: Even if someone's beneath you in status, don't play with their name. That gossip might loop back and hit your rep too.
30.11: Agur sounds like he scrollin' through Twitter in 2024. Self-righteous, disrespectful, sharp-tongued people actin' like they holy. This ain't just generational shade—it's spiritual warning.
30.15: Greed never sleeps. Death. The barren womb. Dry land. Fire. All of 'em want more. And a greedy heart? Just like that. Never full. Never settled.
30.17: That ain't poetic—it's prophetic. Disrespect to your parents don't go unnoticed by heaven.
30.18: Agur marvels at mystery. Some movements in life, love, and nature? Unpredictable and beautiful. He's sayin': "I don't get it—but I respect it."
30.20: Culture can normalize anything. But God ain't moved by how casual we treat sin.
30.21: Power in the wrong hands? Destabilizing. Entitlement with no discipline = chaos.
30.24: Ants: plan ahead. Hyraxes (rock badgers): stay covered. Locusts: move in unity. Lizards: small, but they end up in palaces.
30.29: Some things move like they know who they are. Confidence ain't arrogance when it's grounded in truth and purpose.
30.32: Sometimes the smartest thing to say is nothing. When pride rising or tension brewin'—shut it down before it spills.

31.1: This king had a wise mama, and she said, "Listen, baby." Wisdom starts in the home—and mama ain't sugarcoatin'.
31.3: She keepin' it real: "Don't let lust rob you of legacy." Even kings fall when they chase pleasure over purpose.
31.4: Leaders can't move like everybody else. Getting drunk dulls wisdom, delays judgment, and destroys trust.
31.8: Leadership without justice is just noise. If you got influence, use it to protect, not just profit.
31.10: This woman is rare. A gem, not for show—but for structure. She ain't just valuable—she's foundational.
31.11: She's not just a partner—she's a pillar. Her presence brings him peace, not pressure.
31.13: She's a boss. Multi-skilled. Market-smart. Organized and efficient. Ain't waiting on nobody—she moves with intention.
31.20: Her grind ain't just for herself. She blesses others 'cause she's rooted in compassion.
31.21: Her home is straight. Her style is royalty. She don't fear the future—she prepares for it.
31.23: Her strength upgrades his name. She adds weight to his influence—not by dimming down, but by shining with wisdom.
31.25: She's strong, not hard. She's wise, not loud. She's present, not passive.
31.28: The folks she sacrifices for? They see her. Her impact is so strong, they can't help but honor it.
31.30: Looks fade. Charm can be fake. But a woman who reveres God? She's untouchable.
31.31: Celebrate her out loud. Give credit where credit due—not just in private, but in front of everybody.
